title: When the Garden Burns Anew
premise: Juniper Yarrow poisons himself slowly by profession and hides his guild's ledgers of impossible trades by habit, until a dying courier leaves him a map to the court beneath the mountain and the name of the soul sold there: his mother's. Following the map means betraying the guild that raised him, whose Master traded that soul decades ago and has been feeding Juniper's immunity toward a single poisoned winter feast. Juniper descends, discovers the soul is the seed of the burning garden his mother once kept, and must choose between restoring her and exposing the guild. In the end he steals the soul back, lets the garden burn anew above ground, and testifies against the Master, trading his own invisibility for the truth.
about_author: Ulyana Nakamura is a former pastry chef who spent six years working in hotel kitchens across three countries before turning to fantasy. She writes about food, debt, and the people who taste danger first.

chapters.title: The Taster's Portion
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He samples the prince's birthday feast, catalogues a subtle bitterness only he can taste, and quietly saves a life no one will thank him for. Establishes his routine, his ledgers, and his creed of staying small. Emotional beat: the loneliness of professional invisibility.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He balances the guild's accounts: a bottled echo, a year of borrowed luck, one soul, sold, entry sealed in the Master's hand. He notices the soul's seller signature matches his own family name. Emotional beat: the first crack of dread in a well-ordered life.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Dock Gate
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A frost-bitten courier collapses against him in the fish market, pressing a wax-sealed map and the words 'before the winter finishes falling' before dying. City watch approaches; Juniper flees with the map. Emotional beat: terror and unwilling inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Master Keeps Below
chapters.summary: Master Corvane's POV. He learns of the courier's death and orders the map recovered, revealing he has been seasoning Juniper's immunity doses toward one specific feast. Emotional beat: cold, paternal menace; the reader sees Juniper is both ward and ingredient.

chapters.title: The Map That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He studies the map in his cellar: tunnels beneath the mountain, a sealed court, and a garden symbol he recognizes from his mother's only surviving recipe card. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as purpose.

chapters.title: An Old Debt at the Apothecary
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He seeks out Wren, a disgraced guild archivist who owes him, and trades a favor for translation of the map's script. Wren warns him the court beneath trades in what you cannot afford to lose. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, first act of open rebellion.

chapters.title: The Feast He Was Seasoned For
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the winter court's opening banquet he realizes every immunity dose has built toward a single dish meant to kill the old king and frame the taster. He palms the poison. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Guild of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren covers Juniper's absence in the ledgers and discovers Corvane has been falsifying entries for thirty years, including the sale of a soul named Yarrow. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against documented truth.

chapters.title: Down the Stair of Frosts
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He enters the mountain tunnels, navigating cold that remembers names and doors that open only to hunger. He trades a memory of his father's voice for passage. Emotional beat: the cost of descent made literal.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He reaches a candlelit subterranean court of exiled nobles who trade in souls, seasons, and names. They recognize the map's seal and offer him hospitality with hooks in it. Emotional beat: seductive danger; he is seen here, which is almost a relief.

chapters.title: A Soul Named Yarrow
chapters.summary: The Undercourt Herald's POV. The court's records confirm the soul in their vault is Juniper's mother's, sold by Corvane to secure the guild's charter. The Herald, curious, lets Juniper see the vault door. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The court names its price: not gold, but the ledgers themselves, the guild's whole book of impossible trades. Juniper refuses and is thrown into the frost cells to reconsider. Emotional beat: the trap of choosing between two betrayals.

chapters.title: What Corvane Buried
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Flashback woven with present: thirty years ago he sold a rival gardener's soul to save the guild, and took her son as penance and insurance. He dispatches enforcers down the mountain. Emotional beat: a villain who believes he was merciful.

chapters.title: The Frost Cells
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Imprisoned, he befriends a cell-neighbor, a court scribe who once tasted for the Undercourt and knows a servant's way into the vault. Juniper's taster's discipline becomes survival: he learns to read poison in the prison bread. Emotional beat: resilience, quiet hope.

chapters.title: The Servant's Way
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Escape through the kitchens of the dead court, using his guild skills to pass as staff. The scribe sacrifices her own name to hold the door. Emotional beat: solidarity among the invisible.

chapters.title: The Vault of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Inside the vault he finds his mother's soul kept in a jar of preserved summer, and beside it, dozens of others. He can carry only one. Emotional beat: the agony of a singular choice, and his decision to take hers.

chapters.title: Alarm in the Deep Court
chapters.summary: Herald's POV. The theft is discovered; the court wakes its winter, and the long winter above begins to finish falling early. Enforcers and court hunters converge on the tunnels. Emotional beat: pursuit, escalating dread.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Corvane intercepts him at the mountain's mouth, offering absolution in exchange for the jar and silence. Juniper refuses, and Wren arrives with the falsified ledgers as leverage. Emotional beat: confrontation; the son outgrows the father-figure.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Garden
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He releases the soul at the ruined garden above the mountain; it ignites into green flame, burning away the false winter and the guild's charter magic with it. Corvane's power gutters. Emotional beat: catharsis, grief and joy in one fire.

chapters.title: Testimony of a Taster
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Before the winter court and the guild, Juniper reads the ledgers aloud, naming every impossible trade, including the one made with his mother. He gives up his anonymity forever. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: What Grows in Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The guild is reformed under new, open accounting; Wren is made archivist. Juniper plants the garden's surviving seeds and tastes the first spring dish for a king who now knows his name. Emotional beat: earned belonging.

chapters.title: The Long Winter, Finished Falling
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Epilogue. On the first thaw, a letter arrives from the Undercourt: other souls wait in the vault, and the court remembers who opened the door. Juniper packs the map, his ledgers, and his mother's recipe card. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; the story ends where a larger one begins.
